Introduction
Caffeine (1, 3, 7-trimethylxanthine) in food and beverages, an adenosine antagonist, is the most widely used mood-altering drug in
the world. Caffeine is rapidly absorbed and distributed throughout the body with peak plasma concentrations typically reached 30–
45 min after ingestion. The average half-life of caffeine is 4–6 h. Genetics account for some of the variability in responses to caffeine
and individual differences in caffeine pharmacokinetics.
